periods.public: The panel discusses the necessity of verifying the practical feasibility of the proposals. They agree to investigate infrastructure, staffing, and historical performance to ensure the grant is used effectively.

lines.Servas: Suggests looking at the human element and staffing.
lines.Midori: Expresses concern about the actual purchasing power of the funds.
lines.Kenji: Wants to check the state of shared facilities.
lines.Benjamin: Proposes looking for systemic causes of project delays.
lines.Toshio: Suggests reviewing the actual outcomes of past grants.

lines.Servas: Agrees with the need for a comprehensive check.
lines.Midori: Supports the idea of checking facility costs.
lines.Kenji: Agrees that historical data is useful.
lines.Benjamin: Notes that technical bottlenecks are often hidden.
lines.Toshio: Remains focused on the reliability of the results.

lines.Servas: Finalizes his choice of staffing and secondment records.
lines.Midori: Chooses travel/bench-fees and facility day rates.
lines.Kenji: Chooses instrumentation logs and facility bookings.
lines.Benjamin: Chooses schedule overruns and field site records.
lines.Toshio: Chooses closeout files and repository turnaround.

periods.public: Participants share the general nature of their findings without revealing specific candidate details. They discuss the risks associated with different research environments, such as field sites versus simulations.

lines.Servas: Mentions a shortage of specific technical staff.
lines.Midori: Notes that some subsidies are holding while others are not.
lines.Kenji: Reports issues with equipment maintenance and bookings.
lines.Benjamin: Highlights the volatility of field-based work.
lines.Toshio: Observes that certain project types have better long-term utility.

lines.Servas: Questions if the projects have the necessary hands.
lines.Midori: Wonders how the budget will cover rising costs.
lines.Kenji: Warns about the risk of shared facility downtime.
lines.Benjamin: Suggests avoiding projects prone to external interruptions.
lines.Toshio: Argues for prioritizing projects with proven delivery models.

lines.Servas: Reflects on the fragility of expertise.
lines.Midori: Tries to balance the budget concerns with scientific merit.
lines.Kenji: Emphasizes the need for available infrastructure.
lines.Benjamin: Points out the difference between computational and biological risks.
lines.Toshio: Stresses the importance of tangible deliverables.

periods.public: The candidates are revealed. The panel evaluates each proposal against the discovered constraints regarding staffing, facility availability, and historical success rates before voting.

lines.Servas: Evaluates the staffing needs of the candidates.
lines.Midori: Considers the cost implications for each project.
lines.Kenji: Checks which projects rely on the most stable facilities.
lines.Benjamin: Analyzes the risk of schedule overruns for each.
lines.Toshio: Compares the candidates to the successful past models.

lines.Servas: Notes that some projects lack the necessary technicians.
lines.Midori: Finds one project particularly well-supported by current subsidies.
lines.Kenji: Warns against projects requiring overbooked facilities.
lines.Benjamin: Argues for the stability of simulation-heavy work.
lines.Toshio: Sees high long-term value in a cataloging approach.

lines.Servas: Leans toward the project with the most available support.
lines.Midori: Agrees that the budget fits one project best.
lines.Kenji: Supports the project that avoids the most congested facilities.
lines.Benjamin: Maintains that the lowest risk is in the computational project.
lines.Toshio: Advocates for the project most likely to provide lasting data.

seats.Midori: Concerned with the real-world value of the grant money. She looks for the project whose costs are most likely to be absorbed or subsidized.
seats.Benjamin: Concerned with external interruptions and delays. He evaluates projects based on their susceptibility to environmental or biological setbacks.
seats.Toshio: Concerned with the actual delivery of results. He prioritizes project types that have historically shown the most enduring utility.
seats.Kenji: Concerned with the capacity of shared infrastructure. He weighs the candidates based on the current availability and health of required facilities.
seats.Servas: Concerned with the availability of skilled technical personnel. He focuses on whether the necessary human expertise exists to execute the work.
